subject: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs. VertexAI & OpenServe - OmniHealth
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ayesha Khan <ayesha.khan@omnihealth.com>, Tom Reynolds <treynolds@omnihealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra, laura_bennett
Date: 2026-11-18T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs. VertexAI & OpenServe - OmniHealth

Hi Ayesha / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today




really appreciate the openness on the evaluation criteria. Below is a quick recap from our call so we all have the same next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of pain & goals
- Current pain: unpredictable inference costs and latency spikes impacting the patient triage UI during peak hours.
- Goal: consistent p95 latency < 250ms for short-form prompts (<= 256 tokens), predictable unit cost, and full auditability for PHI-sensitive logs.
- Constraint: deployment must live in their us-east-1 VPC with KMS-managed keys.

Decision criteria (what you told us)
1) Latency & tail behavior (p50/p95/p99) under realistic traffic patterns
2) Integration with VPC + customer-managed KMS
3) Cost per 1k generated tokens at targeted throughput
4) Model output fidelity for clinical summarization tasks (ROUGE/QA checks)
5) Operational controls: rollbacks, canary, and audit logs retention

Competitive positioning (what came up)
- VertexAI: strong managed infra, but flexible VPC integrations may take additional configuration; pricing looks competitive on sustained throughput.
- OpenServe (OSS provider): good latency in single-node tests but lacks enterprise-grade tracing and audit logs out of the box.
- Redwood: focused on predictable serving with built-in KV/prefix caching, model variant fallbacks, and KMS + audit logging in Private deployments.

Open questions you asked us to validate
- Can Redwood run inside your us-east-1 VPC with customer KMS and still provide automated fallbacks? (Yes



we support Private deployments with customer-managed KMS and can configure fallback policies that respect VPC routing.)
- Can we reproduce p95 latency under the test load you described (3k concurrent users simulated over 10-minute bursts)? (We propose a test harness; see test plan attachment.)
- What level of audit log retention (S3/HSM) is possible and what the egress footprint looks like?

Proposed next steps
1) Red team test: Redwood will run a 2-hour simulated burst (3k concurrent over 10-minute cycles) in a staging VPC you provide. Deliverable: p50/p95/p99 latency breakdown + unit-cost estimate. (Owner: rishi_malhotra)
2) Output fidelity check: Redwood to run a 500-sample clinical summarization eval vs. your golden set. (Owner: marissa_cole)
3) Security & procurement: share SOC2 artifacts & KMS key-scope doc with your procurement team. (Owner: laura_bennett)
4) Timeline: run tests this week, goal to share bake-off deck by Friday.

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-summary.pdf (summary + sample config), omnihealth-test-plan.xlsx (test harness steps)

I


'll ping Rishi and Laura to kick off infra access. Thanks


for the results.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0127

From: Ayesha Khan <ayesha.khan@omnihealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Tom Reynolds <treynolds@omnihealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra, laura_bennett
Date: 2026-11-18T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs. VertexAI & OpenServe - OmniHealth

Thanks Marissa




this is great and very aligned to what we discussed. A few clarifications and items from our side:

- Confirmed: we can provision a staging VPC in us-east-1 and provide a temporary KMS key for the tests. Security will need the details of what metadata is logged (headers vs. payload).
- For the fidelity set: we will share the golden 500 summaries by Thursday EOD




they contain de-identified notes.
- Procurement: procurement@omnihealth.com asks for a rough list price and a committed discounted pricing band if we were to go 12-month reserved capacity. Can you share a placeholder?

Open question to Redwood: what




's the expected egress/S3 footprint for a 2-hour stress test (ballpark)? We need that to provision temporary S3 space.

Thanks

Ayesha
Director, Clinical AI Programs
Ayesha.Khan@omnihealth.com

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole, laura_bennett
Cc: Ayesha Khan <ayesha.khan@omnihealth.com>, Tom Reynolds <treynolds@omnihealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T18:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs. VertexAI & OpenServe - OmniHealth

Thanks


> Proposed next steps
> 1) Red team test: Redwood will run a 2-hour simulated burst (3k concurrent over 10-minute cycles) in a staging VPC you provide. Deliverable: p50/p95/p99 latency breakdown + unit-cost estimate. (Owner: rishi_malhotra)

Plan & checklist for infra access
- We need a temporary IAM role with limited permissions (EC2/EKS describe + deploy for our infra container) and an S3 bucket with a put policy limited to test/*. We will not store PHI


- KMS: provide a key ARN scoped to test bucket; we will log key usage but not retain raw payloads.
- Test harness: will generate ~1.5GB of compressed logs for the 2-hour run (ballpark), and another ~200MB of summarized metrics/trace output. Please provision ~5GB to be safe.
- Test config: we will run three model variants (base, quantized-int8, fallback-reduced) to capture cost/latency tradeoffs. We expect to deliver a short report and the raw CSVs.

Open items for OmniHealth to confirm
- IAM role + temporary KMS key + S3 bucket name
- Golden dataset delivery by Thu EOD

I’ll kick off once we have IAM + S3 details.

- Rishi
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ayesha Khan <ayesha.khan@omnihealth.com>, Tom Reynolds <treynolds@omnihealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@omnihealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra, laura_bennett, stephanie_nguyen
Date: 2026-11-19T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs. VertexAI & OpenServe - OmniHealth

Appreciate the quick turn, Ayesha



Procurement placeholder pricing
- Placeholder for 2-week evaluation (test only): no charge (we cover test run compute for the bake-off).
- Placeholder for 12-month reserved capacity (example band): $18k - $30k / month for the committed capacity tier that meets your 3k concurrent workload; final price will depend on model mix & QPS profile. We’ll provide a more formal quote after the test when we have the exact model/mix numbers.

Next steps & timeline
- Today: OmniHealth to share IAM role ARN, KMS test key ARN, and S3 bucket name.
- Thu EOD: receive golden dataset (500 samples).
- Fri: Redwood runs 2-hour stress test in your staging VPC and returns p50/p95/p99, cost estimate, and fidelity eval summary by EOD Friday.
- Early next week: follow-up call to go over results and potential reserved pricing/terms.

If procurement needs an MSA template or SOC2, Laura will share. I’ve attached a short bake-off summary and the proposed test plan for your review.

Best,
Marissa
